thread:
Anya K: bringing up reranker v2-small-int8 on prod-lite, seeing ~3.2% absolute MRR drop vs float32 baseline on the longtail slice. NDCG for head queries is flat. Anyone seen this pattern with kv-packing or tokenizer differences? :thinking_face:
Samir R: did you run with the same candidate ordering/normalization as the baseline? small reorders can tank MRR on tail.
Anya K: yes, same candidate set from prod logs. eval harness pipeline used during onboarding strips doc-level metadata though — could be mismatch. Also ran with batch_size=128 and kv_pack enabled.
Tess P: quick thought — PTQ can change softmax sharpness. NDCG less sensitive to top-of-list shuffles than MRR for single-relevant queries.
Michael L: +1 on softmax. also check seed + cudnn nondet. we've seen small deterministic diffs that amplify after argmax on short candidate lists.
Anya K: good points. I'll rerun with kv_pack disabled and set deterministic flags. command I'm running now:
```
python -m evals.rerank \
  --model v2-small-int8 \
  --candidates ./prod_candidates.json \
  --slice longtail \
  --batch_size 16 \
  --kv_pack False \
  --seed 42 \
  --deterministic True
```
Devon C: also capture logits and compare softmax temperatures. if quant shifts logits, we can compute KL between float and int8 outputs per-query.
Anya K: good idea — will log per-query KL and top1/top3 flips. hoping to isolate whether it's calibration or ranking ordering.
deploy-bot: ci pipeline note: prod-lite pinned to runtime-3.2, make sure local build uses same kernels. :robot_face:
Samir R: if it's ordering flips on short lists, try rerun with candidate expansion (pad with decoys) to see if MRR sensitivity reduces.
Tess P: also sanity-check tokenizer: truncation side and whitespace normalization can change query/document pairings. small tokenizer mismatch -> big ranking swing.
Anya K: plan: (1) rerun with kv_pack off + deterministic, (2) capture logits + KL per-query, (3) run candidate-expansion probe, (4) diff tokenizer preproc. I'll post results in ~2h. :rocket:
Michael L: thanks — if you want, I can spin a dedicated GPU to speed the dense eval.
Anya K: appreciate it, Michael. pinging @eval-bot to schedule a slice job if needed.
eval-bot: scheduled slice job 8271 for v2-small-int8 longtail. ETA ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Anya K: noted. thanks everyone.
